subject: Cognitive Science
title: Essentialist Thinking
description: A fast breakdown of Essentialist Thinking for builders.

hook.text: People feel a sweater once worn by a killer is "contaminated." They sense an invisible essence.

buildup.text: Psychological essentialism is the belief that categories have a hidden inner nature that makes them real.

discovery.text: Susan Gelman found that even preschoolers think animals have an internal essence that determines behavior.

twist.text: Essentialism works for gold (it really has an atomic essence) but fails for race or gender.

climax.text: Treating social categories as "natural kinds" fuels discrimination by making groups feel fixed.

punchline.text: Not every category has a hidden essence.

quiz.question: What is psychological essentialism?
options: The belief that categories have a hidden inner nature
The idea that all categories are artificial
